records.name: Human Rights Coalition
records.summary: A grassroots group run by people in prison and their families. It campaigns against solitary confinement and harsh prison conditions, pushes for fairer sentencing and release, and helps people inside prepare for life after prison.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a campaign through the Get Involved form, come to the monthly Toxic Prisons Campaign meetings or a Thursday letter-writing night, or read its quarterly magazine, The MOVEMENT.

schedule.text: Monthly Toxic Prisons Campaign meetings on Mondays, 6 to 7 pm, and monthly letter-writing nights on Thursdays, 6 to 8 pm, as listed on the events page.

cost.text: No event fee is listed. The site asks for donations.

first_step.how: Use the RSVP form linked on hrcoalition.org/events to sign up for the next Monday Toxic Prisons meeting or Thursday letter-writing night, or fill in the Get Involved form to join a campaign.
first_step.basis: Both event series use public sign-up forms, and the Get Involved form is open to anyone. The page does not say the meetings are open to the public, so the rating stays at 3 instead of 4.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Thursday letter-writing night runs 6 to 8 pm, with snacks and drinks provided, and you sign up through a form to get the location. The Monday Toxic Prisons Campaign meetings run 6 to 7 pm, you RSVP through a form first, and the group's program director leads them. The site does not say how many people usually come.
first_visit_tips: RSVP first: the Monday meetings use an RSVP form, and the letter-writing location is sent only after you sign up.
Snacks and drinks are provided at letter-writing nights.

records.notes: The events page heading reads Upcoming, but its newest listed dates are July 2026, so status and last_sign_of_life rest on that July 2026 evidence. No page names a meeting place or says whether the events are open to the public. The contact page lists social handles that do not match this group's name, so they were not recorded. The reentry page lists job training pathways as coming soon.

records.name: Let's Circle Up
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches and practices restorative justice, an approach focused on healing and taking responsibility for harm. Its work reaches prisons and Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Ask through the contact form about its Intro Restorative Justice Workshop, a ten-session course with a two-day mini version. Volunteers can fill in an interest form to help with inside workshops, and the group holds a yearly A Call to End Harm event. You can also donate or buy its book.

schedule.text: A ten-session Intro Restorative Justice Workshop, with a two-day mini version. The site does not post dates for these workshops.

cost.text: No fee is listed. The site asks for donations.

first_step.how: Send a message through the contact form on letscircleup.org to ask when the next Intro Restorative Justice Workshop runs and how to join.
first_step.basis: The site names an Intro workshop, a contact form and a volunteer form, but it does not say who the workshop is for, when it runs, or what it costs. Volunteer roles inside prisons go through an interest form and a reply.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Intro workshop is a ten-session course, and a two-day mini version is also offered. The site does not say who joins, how long each session runs, or whether there is a fee, so ask before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Email info@letscircleup.org or use the contact form first; the site lists no phone number or street address.
Ask about the location and accessibility before you go, since the site gives no details on either.

records.notes: The history page's newest dated item is 2024 (a restorative justice course at a Philadelphia college), with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is set and activity since then is unconfirmed. The get-involved page shows an event whose flyer text could not be read; its file name mentions November 2026, which is not counted as evidence. Volunteer work inside workshops takes place at SCI-Phoenix in Collegeville, outside the city. The two addresses come from IRS records. The site lists no street address, and the Apt address may be a home, so check before showing it.

records.name: Mill Creek Community Partnership
records.summary: Neighbors working to strengthen the Mill Creek area of West Philadelphia through free art and education programs, community events, and voter information.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free art class, workshop, festival, or community meal, volunteer through the Join Our Mission form, or book the Art Bus for a block party or community event.

schedule.text: Over 30 free community events a year, according to the group's site. The Art Bus runs pop-up art activities from early April through late October, and the F.A.T.O.E. art programming runs year-round at host sites.

cost.text: Programs and community events are free, and donations are optional.

access.notes: A past event page (Kwanzaa FEST 2025) says it is handicap accessible and has free street parking. The venue is not named, and the site gives no other access details.

first_step.how: RSVP through the form on the upcoming events page for a free workshop such as the Survival Training series, or send the Volunteer or partner inquiry form at mccpcommunity.com/get-involved.
first_step.basis: Free events are open to the public, the group lists a volunteer inquiry form, an email and a phone number, but the site does not post a regular schedule or say what a first event is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most events are free workshops, festivals, meals, or community days, and some ask you to RSVP first. The site does not say how long events run, who usually attends, or what you do at them, so check the listing or call before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call 267.225.7351 or email mccpcommunity@gmail.com for the time and place, since some event listings show neither.
Ask about physical access before you go; the site notes handicap accessibility for only one past event.

records.notes: The upcoming events page shows a Kwanzaa FEST 2026 save the date (Saturday, December 26, 2026) and a Kwanzaa FEST 2025 listing with no month, so status stays probably_active rather than active. The site says the group was established in 2005; its footer shows 2035, which looks like a typo. The community page lists Candidate N Community under community engagement. Its content was not checked, so a reviewer should confirm it is nonpartisan voter education before this record goes live. The 1500 Chestnut St address is an IRS mailing address with a suite number, not a meeting place.

records.name: Philadelphia Rebelz Basketball
records.summary: A North Philadelphia basketball program for young players. It fields teams, runs coaching, hosts clinics and tournaments, and gives away gear to the community.
records.what_you_do: Try out for an AAU team (16U for players born in 2008, 17U for players born in 2007), play in the Grindhouse League, or come to a free gear giveaway, clinic, or 3v3 tournament. Some events are for 18 and over or invitation only.

schedule.text: Teams, clinics and tournaments are announced on the site. No regular weekly practice schedule is published.

cost.text: The register page lists no fee. Payment is requested only after a coach selects you.

first_step.how: Fill in the registration form at rebelz.club/register for the 16U or 17U AAU team, then attend the tryout when the dates are sent to you.
first_step.basis: Team places need a registration, a tryout and a coach's selection before payment, so this is not a drop-in. The register form itself is public.
first_step.what_to_expect: Coaches teach the basics of the game and focus on teamwork and discipline, and the teams play in competitive events. The site does not say how often teams practice, where they meet, or what a tryout involves.
first_visit_tips: Check your birth year first: the AAU teams are 16U (born 2008) and 17U (born 2007).
Ask where practices and tryouts are held, since the site gives only a mailing address.
Tryout dates are sent to you after you register, so watch for a message.

records.notes: The newest dated items are the 2025 UnityKlassic (invitation only, 18 and over) and the 2025 RebelZ Clinic. Neither has a month, so no last_sign_of_life is set. The STEM page lists drone flight and FAA Part 107 training, a REBELZ Chess Collective, app development and computer science, with no ages, places, costs or times, so no record was made for them. Venues named on the site (SixthMan Center, The Christian Academy, Christy Rec Center) have no addresses, so they are not listed as locations.

records.name: Philly Autism Kickback
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that holds a yearly Dave & Buster's event and takes donations on its website.
records.what_you_do: Watch the group's social media pages for the next Dave & Buster's event, or give through the Make a Donation page on its website.

schedule.text: A yearly Dave & Buster's event, as the group describes it. No date for the next one is posted.

first_step.how: Follow the group's Instagram or Facebook page to hear when the next Dave & Buster's event opens for registration, or use the Make a Donation page on its website.
first_step.basis: The yearly event is listed publicly, but registration for the last one was closed and the site lists no other way in. Three of its pages returned 404 errors.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group calls the Dave & Buster's gathering an annual event, and the page for the last one shows a noon start in Philadelphia. The site does not describe what happens at the event or who it is for.

records.notes: The about-us, events and contact-us pages on phillyautismkickback.org returned 404 errors, so only the home page could be read. A web search for a 2026 Dave & Buster's event found no listing for this group, so the newest dated evidence is still the November 22, 2025 event. Status is active only because that event falls within the last 12 months.

records.name: Simply Music
records.summary: A Philadelphia music nonprofit for children, teens and adults. It offers in-person and online music classes, plus recitals, workshops and student CD releases.
records.what_you_do: Take an in-person or online music class, ask the studio how to enroll, and come to recitals, workshops and student CD releases.

schedule.text: In-person classes run on Tuesday and Wednesday, 12 to 7 pm, as listed on the site.

cost.text: No tuition is listed. The site takes donations through PayPal.

first_step.how: Call (267) 701-2359 or use the contact form on simplymusicinc.com to ask about enrolling in a Tuesday or Wednesday class, in person or online.
first_step.basis: Classes and online options are listed, but the site does not explain how to enroll, how long classes run, what they cost, or who they suit, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: In-person classes meet on weekday afternoons and evenings, and online classes are marked as available. The studio also holds recitals, workshops and events for students. The site does not say how long a class lasts, what it costs, or how new students are placed.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come: office hours are listed as Monday to Friday, 11 am to 6 pm, with Saturdays by appointment and Sundays closed.
If travel is hard, ask about an online class; the site marks online classes as available.

records.notes: The events page lists no years, so there is no dated evidence newer than probably_active. The Q&A page has no entries. The about page gives no founding year, class lengths, tuition or enrollment steps. The end time on the class hours has no AM or PM marker on the site; 12 to 7 pm follows the tier 1 reading.

records.name: SAS Project
records.summary: Gives away gender-affirming clothing for free to trans and queer adults, and offers community care and mutual aid.
records.what_you_do: Ask for clothing or community resources through the online Get Support form, drop off clean donated clothing at 3675 Market St on weekdays, or sign up to help through the Volunteer Interest Form, for example by sorting clothes or setting up events. The group also runs pop-up closets and workshops.

schedule.text: Donation drop-off at 3675 Market St is Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm. Weekends are by appointment only.

cost.text: Clothing is free, and pop-up closets use a sliding scale.

first_step.how: Fill in the online Get Support form on sasproject.org to ask for affirming clothing or help finding community resources. It takes about 3 to 5 minutes.
first_step.basis: Help starts with a form that the team reviews before offering anything, and the page says a request does not guarantee help. The volunteer route also starts with a form and a reply, and no open drop-in time is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: A request is a short online form, and the team reviews it and replies later, not right away. Help depends on stock, funding, program availability and team capacity. The group also holds pop-up closets and workshops, but the site gives no dates and does not describe what a visit is like.
first_visit_tips: Send only what the form needs: the group asks you not to include ID, Social Security numbers, medical records, immigration papers or financial account details.
Expect a reply later; the form is not watched around the clock.
For donations, bring clean, gently used clothing only. Undergarments and heavily worn items are not accepted.

records.notes: Two contact emails appear on the group's site: info@sasproject.org (on the FAQ and Give Support pages) and thesasprojectinfo@gmail.com (on the Let's Collaborate button, and carried from tier 1). The record keeps the Gmail address. The FAQ says to write to info@sasproject.org for questions, so a reviewer should confirm which one is current. The FAQ says the program does not serve minors and is designed for adults. No minimum age number is written, so none is recorded. The Collaborators and Media pages were not read. No event dates are given.
